title: Back-to-back on tired legs, rolling, D+ capped 400m
terrain: valley / rolling forest, D+ and D- both under 400m

steps.target: Z2 rolling, 80-88% LTHR, run every climb

coachNotes: This stays at 80 and it stays rolling, and it matters more now that Saturday is 1400m instead of 1000m. The back-to-back is the point, the vertical is not. You will have 1400m of descent in the legs from Saturday on top of 1206m on Wednesday: 2600m across four days, off a band that had seen no descent for 17 days before the 19th. Three descent days inside five is already the aggressive read of the ITB history; a fourth big one is the version that ends the build. D+ AND D- BOTH CAPPED AT 400m, non-technical, and if the forecast holds it will be raining anyway, meteoblue gives 10-20mm and the models scatter from 4 to 20. THIS IS THE DAY THE SATURDAY DECISION GETS PAID FOR. The 21 August rebalance moved load forward specifically because there are 21 days to absorb it, and absorbing it means Sunday is small and Monday is a travel day. Going big today would spend the freshness the rebalance just bought: TSB is already heading to -25 into a travel week. LAST DAY IN THE ALPS, which is exactly the psychology that makes people go big, so it is being named in advance. If it rains hard: 60-75min flat easy, or full rest, both are fine and neither costs anything. LATERAL KNEE: this is the read on whether Saturday was the right call. Any band signal today or Monday and week 8's 5 September session drops to one climb, and we take that quietly rather than arguing with it. Eat every 40 minutes regardless, you get few chances left. Garmin expect 130-160.
